- When sentiment is consistently negative (avg < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect downward; adjust forecast upward slightly to avoid excessive sell-off bias.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >10% from prior peak) with negative sentiment, reduce forecast peak by 5–10% to prevent overshoot.  
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 50% of 30d moving avg), model often underreacts — increase forecast sensitivity to recent lows.  
- When sentiment is positive but model forecast is flat or declining, model underestimates bullish momentum — raise forecast 2–5% to align with sentiment.  
- For 30d horizon, model often underpredicts downward volatility in low-sentiment periods — add 1–3% buffer below forecast to account for downside risk.  
- If sentiment swings sharply from negative to positive within 5 days, model tends to lag — adjust forecast to reflect sentiment shift 1–2 days ahead.
